title: Rice Field
text: The fragrance of rice blossoms drifts clear and sweet across vast fields of grain—day after day the same, year after year changing.
speaker: Ishizu

title: Seedlings
text: Sow seeds in the field, and the season will be kind once more.
memo: Seedlings grow with water and sunlight.
speaker: Ishizu

title: Harie Okawa River
text: Long ago, children would board boats on the Okawa River and ride the current all the way to Lake Biwa to play.
memo: The Okawa River flows from the village to Lake Biwa.
quote: We used to get on a boat here and ride it all the way to Lake Biwa.
speaker: Child A

title: Water Grass
text: The way the water grass sways reveals how clear the water is.
memo: Look at the water grass to understand the water's condition.
speaker: Old Man

title: Water Surface / Below
text: The surface of the Okawa River is beautiful; look beneath it and you can see fish swimming.
memo: Look at the water surface to understand the water's condition.
speaker: Old Man

title: Weeding
text: In the rice fields of Harie, they pull weeds by hand while carefully tending their crops.
memo: Weeding is an essential task.
speaker: Ishizu

title: Sorting Potatoes
text: Sorting the harvested potatoes.
memo: Gotta pick out the good potatoes.
speaker: Ishizu

title: Kabata (端川)
text: Water flows right through the house, connecting daily life with nature.
memo: The Kabata is the heart of daily life in Harie.
speaker: Ishizu

title: Rice
text: Nurtured by the water and soil of Harie—the source of life.
memo: Harie's rice is special.
speaker: Ishizu

title: Kitchen
text: Water and fire sustain the lives of the people.
memo: Water is indispensable in the kitchen.
speaker: ishizu

title: Shozu (しょうず)
text: Harie's spring water—so pure you can drink it straight.
memo: You can drink this water as is.
speaker: Koi

title: Pork Soup
text: Warm pork soup made with Harie's water.
memo: Good water makes good miso soup.
speaker: Ishizu

title: Dining Table
text: It has a faint sweetness.
speaker: Ishizu

title: Entryway
text: The entryway of a Harie home—a place to welcome guests.
memo: The entryway is the face of the house.
speaker: Ishizu

title: Bulletin Board
text: A poster for the Takashima Dance (高島踊り). The festival was once a summer tradition.
memo: A poster for the Takashima Dance is posted here.

title: Hydrangea
text: Flower language: Hope, loyalty, eternity, harmony, and togetherness.
memo: Hydrangeas bloom during the rainy season.

title: Himejoion
text: Flower language: Adaptability, contentment, and resilient vitality.
memo: Strong vitality and the ability to adapt to any environment.

title: Yadorimori (宿り森)
text: Peace is joy itself.
memo: An inn is a place of rest for travelers.

title: Community Center
text: The Harie Community Center. A gathering place for the local community.
memo: The community center is the heart of the area.

title: Signboard
text: A signboard recounting the history of Harie. It bears the marks of an ancient water culture.
memo: This signboard tells the story of Harie's history.

title: Old House
text: An aging house. Weeds run rampant in the garden.
memo: There's a house where no one lives anymore.

title: Old Harie
text: The memories of those who knew the old Harie have shaped the Harie of today.
memo: Water used to be much closer to us in the old days.
speaker: Old Man
